newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsuzuka denies specifying dlr intervention level.
newsitem.headline: Mitsuzuka denies specifying dlr intervention level.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka on Monday denied having made reference to a specific dollar/yen level at which the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would conduct dollar-selling intervention in the foreign exchange market.
"Neither I nor other cabinet ministers have made any specific references to intervention levels," Mitsuzuka said.

His remarks were made in response to a question on whether Mitsuzuka had told a cabinet ministers' meeting on Friday that the BOJ is ready to intervene if the dollar rises to the 127 yen or 128 level.

On Saturday, the Japanese daily Mainichi Shimbun reported that Mitsuzuka said at a meeting of cabinet ministers on Friday that Japan will act in the currency markets when the dollar rises to 127 to 128 yen.
The Mainichi report quoted Mitsuzuka as saying: "Our understanding is that the dollar at 127 or 128 yen is an excessive depreciation of the yen. It is necessary to deal with such exchange rates."
